title: Measured coverage of the frozen-rule retention interval on the door3 classifier rung
statement: Measured evidence only. For the frozen door3 rung n_per_class = 15 (classifier seed 101, four cells, D-exchange seed 7), population references by two independent composite Gauss-Legendre routes agree to 1.1e-16: eta = 0.893663, sigma = 0.235410, proxy population value 0.967064 (gap 0.073402). Over 2000 independent evaluation samples per size (SeedSequence 20260905), the 95% Wald interval covers eta with frequency 0.913, 0.934, 0.953, 0.949 at n = 100, 300, 1000, 3000 (SE about 0.005-0.006); SD(eta_hat) matches sigma/sqrt(n) at every size; sigma_hat/sigma has relative RMSE 0.167 -> 0.029; n * bias is about 0.3; the plug-in studentized statistic has skew +1.06 at n = 100 (population-sigma studentized: -0.30), explaining the small-n shortfall; the interval covers the proxy population value with frequency 0.046 at n = 100 and 0 beyond; no interval left [0, 1]; no cell was empty.
assumptions: population quantities are deterministic 1-D quadrature of the reference Gaussian mixture with cell boundaries located by bisection; integration error is the disagreement of two routes plus an analytic tail bound, not a rigorous bound
Monte Carlo coverage with deterministic seeds; measured, never theorem authority; nothing is claimed about coverage below n = 1000 beyond the recorded numbers
one frozen rule only; no statement about other rungs, other K, or refitted rules

audit replication 5 Sep 2026: the rule was rebuilt from the example module and its cuts mapped through the logit to quadratic roots in x, so p_b and m_b are Gaussian-CDF differences; the recorded population values are reproduced to rounding (and the researcher's full-precision artifact to <= 2e-15) by two quadratures agreeing to 4e-15; fresh seeds (SeedSequence 20260906, 4000 replicates) give coverage 0.918, 0.937, 0.952, 0.946, n*bias about 0.3 and population-studentized skew -0.30 at n = 100 — consistent

audit boundary probes: rung n_per_class = 300 (eta = 0.9716, sigma = 0.0532) covers 0.896, 0.935, 0.940, 0.947 and its interval still contains the proxy value (gap 0.0022) with frequency 0.94 at n = 100 and 0.38 at n = 3000; in the two-atom sigma^2 = 0 law and the atomless eta = 0 law the interval is conservative (coverage 0.994-0.9995 with width O(1/n), eta_hat >= eta always), never liberal

proof_location.section: O6. Frozen-rule scalar retention: plug-in asymptotics and a consistent variance

role: falsification experiment for O6.2-O6.4, run before the proof was trusted; did not falsify
warning: Measured coverage is not a proof (packet rule). The n = 100 under-coverage is a recorded second-order effect, not a counterexample to the first-order theorem. The proxy-exclusion statement of O6.5 is asymptotic: at the rung 300 the proxy gap sits inside the interval for most of the sizes tested.
